result.concerns: 1) Swift was not compiled here. Points a reviewer should watch on the first Apple Watch CI run: URL.host() (iOS 16+) and Link in SettingsView, the Sendable InstalledSchedule struct crossing the detached task, String(format:locale:) with %lld and Int, and the new protocol requirements on every WatchSnapshotSession implementation (both fakes were updated). 2) The new ios CI steps are unverified on a macOS runner: `xcodebuild archive … CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` with CODE_SIGN_STYLE Automatic and an unsubstituted ${BINARIO_APPLE_TEAM_ID} in CI, the BinarioWatch scheme tests on the integrated project (the standalone harness runs the same tests green today), and `plutil -extract … raw` output for booleans ("false"); if a command needs adjusting, .github/ci-inputs-lock.json must be re-hashed in the same change. The step also assumes Xcode honours INFOPLIST_KEY_ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption; it asserts the key in the built plists, so a failure there would be visible, not silent. 3) The GTFS artifact was rebuilt on Linux; its page bytes differ from a macOS rebuild (documented behaviour), CI compares rows via verify_ios_gtfs_rebuild.py. 4) Owner actions recorded in APP_STORE_SUBMISSION.md and APPLE_PLATFORM_READINESS.md: export BINARIO_APPLE_TEAM_ID before generating; register App IDs/App Group; host PRIVACY.md at a public URL with data controller and contact; confirm and record the seven licences still null in binario_gtfs_source_policy_v1.json (ARST, SBB/OTD, EAV, HŽPP, Trenord, SNCF, Trentino) and answer content rights accordingly; refresh the GTFS packs before the submission build (seven packs end 2026-12-12/13) and plan a monthly cadence; check name availability ("Binario Orari" fallback); capture iPhone and mandatory Apple Watch screenshots. 5) Design deviations stated in the items: item 8 did not add `licence` to the Android manifest.json (iOS reads the reviewed, fingerprinted policy); item 10 keeps freshness UNKNOWN on the wire (shared v1 contract) and maps on the Watch; item 9 shows "Disattivata" whenever sharing is off, which hides the clear-confirmation status by design (R4:L-I-3); item 2 used environment substitution rather than an xcconfig, so .gitignore is untouched. 6) Two of my commits were amended in this worktree before any push (item 4 message typo; item 6 test mutation strengthened after the first run left two failures uncaught because a pipeline masked the exit status; the final tree and all commits are green).

findings.description: testBundledInstallerFastPathDoesNotTrustASameSizeCorruptCache is a safety test for the new fast path, not a regression test: with the old hashFile() fast path the same-size garbage cache is also rejected and reinstalled, so the test passes with and without the fix. The behavioural change (no re-hash on launch) is guarded only by the static Python check that asserts hashFile is gone. Acceptable given 'static only' for Swift, but the report should not imply the Swift test proves the fix.
findings.suggested_fix: Advisory: keep the test (it protects the new path); optionally assert in the Swift test that a valid same-size cache is returned without a reinstall (e.g. compare file modification date or inode before/after install) so the fast path itself is exercised.

findings.description: loadSchedule now validates the 26 MB index three times at launch: BundledGTFSScheduleInstaller.validatesDatabase, then sourcePacks() and coveredCatalogStationIDs() each open a new read-only connection and re-run validate() including PRAGMA quick_check(1) (a full page scan). This is consistent with the per-query pattern in load(), runs off the main actor and is far cheaper than the removed pure-Swift SHA-256, so it is not a regression, but it is avoidable work on the launch path the package is trying to shorten.
findings.suggested_fix: Advisory: a single internal helper that opens one connection, validates once and reads both the pack table and the covered-station set would halve the launch-time quick_check cost; not required for merge.

findings.description: isPaired/isWatchAppInstalled are evaluated only when a publish directive executes, and WCSessionAdapter does not forward sessionWatchStateDidChange(_:). If the user pairs a Watch or installs the Watch app while the iPhone app is running, the pending operation stays pending (status .notPaired) until the next search or launch. Behaviour before the change was equivalent (operation kept pending with .failed), so no regression; noted because the new status now looks final.
findings.suggested_fix: Advisory: implement sessionWatchStateDidChange(_:) in WCSessionAdapter and call activationHandler?(.activated) when isPaired && isWatchAppInstalled becomes true, so the state machine re-issues the pending operation; add a FakeSession test for it.

findings.description: indexEnded(before:) uses MAX(last_service_date) over packs with trips, i.e. the index counts as ended only after the latest pack (Trentino, 2027-06-25 in the committed artifact). Between 2026-12-12 (seven packs end) and that date a query for a station the index never served still reads 'no journey', while routes inside an ended pack correctly read 'expired' via packsEnded. This matches the plan wording ('the index's last service date') and the picker now flags unserved stations, so it is a documented limitation rather than a defect.
findings.suggested_fix: Advisory only: no code change needed; the owner note about refreshing before 2026-12-12 already covers the practical case. If stricter behaviour is wanted later, use MIN over packs with trips, but that would mislabel still-valid Trentino/SNCF/EAV routes as expired.

findings.description: Three macOS-only assumptions in the new ios job steps cannot be verified here and were correctly flagged by the colleague: (1) `plutil -extract … raw` printing booleans as `false`; (2) actool writing a top-level CFBundleIconName into the embedded watchOS app's Info.plist (the step asserts it); (3) `xcodebuild test -scheme BinarioWatch` on the integrated, companion-dependent Watch app installed alone on the paired watch simulator. XcodeGen leaves `${BINARIO_APPLE_TEAM_ID}` literal when the variable is unset (CI runs xcodegen directly), which xcodebuild evaluates to an empty DEVELOPMENT_TEAM; with CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO that is fine. Any failure here is visible, not silent.
findings.suggested_fix: Advisory: watch the first Apple Watch CI run after push; if a command needs adjusting, re-hash the two locked run steps in .github/ci-inputs-lock.json in the same change (tests/test_verify_ci_pinning.py will refuse a stale lock).
